 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 20-06-2022 at about 7.35 p.m., the petitioner was a pedestrian and in order to cross the road, he was standing carefully, by following all the traffic rules, near Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 service road, Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Subash Nagara,
Bengaluru District, Karnataka.
At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-04-HN- 1470 came from Nelamangala to Bengaluru, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering the human life, recklessly, unmindfully, without following the traffic rules and without observing the movement of pedestrians and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Matrushree Hospital, thereafter he was shifted to Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was student and also working as electrician and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, the petitioner who was a motorcycle rider in NH-48 had parked his bike on the road side and had jumped the barricade to pass urinals in the service road.

After passing the urinals near a tree in the service road, the petitioner who was in a hurry to cross the road did not notice the respondent's bike coming on the service road and ran towards the NH-48.
The respondent was driving his motorcycle with helmet and all safety measures in the service road, at about 30 to 40 km speed, along with a pillion rider.

The petitioner became a sudden obstacle to the respondent's bike,
for which the respondent could not control his vehicle and dashed the petitioner, who was in hurry to cross the road.
Both the petitioner and respondent have sustained injuries.

Further it is contended that,
the general public immediately gave water to the petitioner and respondent, started scolding the petitioner for rushing to cross the road.
The respondent being an innocent, humble, law abiding citizen did not claim any damages from the petitioner, as he was already in the pain of his injuries.
Taking undue advantage of the innocence of respondent, the petitioner has now come up with the present false petition, in order to grab money from the respondent.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 20-06-2022 at about 7.35 p.m.,
due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motorcycle, bearing registration No. KA-04-HN-1470 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.

the respondent has got examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked one document as Ex.R.1.

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner

that, on 20-06-2022 at about 7.35 p.m., near Bengaluru-Tumkur NH- 48 service road, Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Subash Nagara, Bengaluru District, Karnataka, when the petitioner was standing and waiting to cross the road, carefully, by following all the traffic rules, at that time the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-HN-1470 came from Nelamangala to Bengaluru, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without following the traffic rules, without observing the movement of pedestrians and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was Maneesh K.S vs Umesha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135360493/

But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of statement, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is true copy of reply to notice issued under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.9 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.10 is discharge summary,
Ex.P.11 are prescriptions (total 9), Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total 11), Ex.P.13 is medical advance receipt, Ex.P.14 is authorization letter, Ex.P.15 are case-sheets (total 2), Ex.P.16 are x-rays (total 4),

Ex.P.17 is OPD record and Ex.P.18 is x-ray.
11.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN-1470 and dashing the same to the petitioner who was crossing the road.
Further it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg in the said accident.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, marked as Ex.P.9, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN-1470 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, there is no dispute with regard date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 04-HN-1470 in the alleged accident.
But, the respondent has denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident.

Further, he has taken specific defence that, the accident in question has occurred solely due to negligence of the petitioner himself and there was no fault on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HN-1470.

Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the petitioner being the rider of motorcycle on NH-48 road, parked his motorcycle beside the road,
jumped the barricade to pass urinals in the service road and after passing urinals, the petitioner in a hurry to cross the road did not notice the motorcycle of the respondent proceeding on the service road and suddenly ran towards NH-48 road, due to which the respondent could not control his vehicle and dashed the petitioner.
In order to establish the said contentions, the respondent has examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked 6 photographs of place of accident as Ex.R.1.
The respondent in his examination-in-chief affidavit has reiterated the contentions taken in his written statement.

Except the self serving statements of the respondent/R.W.1, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
But, the admissions given by the petitioner/P.W.1 in his cross-examination, clearly establishes that, there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner in the cause of accident.

The petitioner in his Maneesh K.S vs Umesha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135360493/
4 cross-examination has clearly admitted that, the accident has taken place on service road of Tumkur-Bengaluru National Highway road and at both the ends of the said road there is 3 feet concrete barricade.

sentences.text: Further, he has clearly admitted that, to attend the nature call, he had parked his motorcycle on the national highway and in order to reach the service road he jumped the said concrete barricade and crossed the service road and after attending the nature call when he was returning towards his parked motorcycle by crossing the service road, the rider of offending motorcycle dashed against him and thereby caused the accident.
Further, he has clearly admitted that, to attend the nature call he had jumped the concrete barricade and there were no zebra cross marks in the place of accident to cross the road.
The above admissions clearly establishes the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
But, there is no cogent and corroborative evidence placed on record to show that, the accident has taken place due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, at the relevant point of time of accident, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04- HN-1470 was riding his motorcycle with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and carrying three pillion riders on the said motorcycle.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.9 has clearly stated that, at the time of accident the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HN-1470 was carrying three pillion riders and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the said rider and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the said road.

Further, it is clearly stated in the said charge-sheet that, at the time of accident the rider of offending motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the said vehicle was not insured.

It is pertinent to note that, no where in the evidence or during the cross- examination of P.W.1, the respondent has asserted or contended that, the rider of his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HN-1470 was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the said vehicle was having valid insurance, as on the date of accident.

Further, except the self serving statements of the respondent/R.W.1, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent to show that, as the time of accident, the rider of offending motorcycle was riding the same slowly, by following all the traffic rules and regulations and there was no negligence on his part.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place at the middle of 26 wide Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 service road, near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Subash Nagara, Bengaluru District, Karnataka due to dashing of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-HN-1470 to the petitioner, who was pedestrian and crossing the road

. Further it clearly speaks that, at a distance of 6 feet from the place of accident, towards the North side, there is a barricade and at a distance of 20 feet from the place of accident, towards Southern side, there is a road divider.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-HN-1470 and no other vehicle was involved in the said accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.9, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN-1470.

Admittedly,

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

But, the petitioner has unequivocally admitted in his cross-examination that, to attend the nature call he had parked his motorcycle on the national highway and in order to reach the service road he jumped the concrete barricade installed at both the ends of the said national highway and after attending the nature call he was returning towards his parked motorcycle by crossing the service road, from the place where there were no zebra cross marks to cross the road.

The above admissions given by the petitioner clearly establishes the negligence of the petitioner and it clearly goes to show that, the petitioner was not diligent and taken required care and caution while crossing the public road and thereby contributed in the cause of accident.
If the petitioner had taken required care and caution while using the public road, having proper lookout at the movement of vehicles on the said road, the accident could not have occurred.

On the other hand, if the rider of offending motorcycle had rode his motorcycle slowly or in moderate speed, with due care and caution, following the traffic rules and regulations, he could have avoided the said accident.
The rider of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and observe traffic rules and regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.

Further,
the oral and documentary evidence available on record by both the sides clearly goes to show that,
the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle is at higher side, than that of the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, saddling contributory negligence of 70% on the part of the rider of offending vehicle and 30% on the part of the petitioner would be justified.
14.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 case sheets (total 2), Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 4), Ex.P.17 OPD record and Ex.P.18 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg in the said accident.

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent to show that,
the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN-1470 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 20-06-2022 at about 7:35 p.m., on Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 service road, near Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Subash Nagara,
Bengaluru District, Karnataka, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN- 1470.
But, the petitioner has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle.
For the reasons stated supra it is held that, there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner to the extent of 30% in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident has taken place due to contributory rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle,
bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN- 1470 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record by the petitioner clearly speaks that, he has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.
In the petition, his age is shown as 19 years, as on the date of accident.
Likewise, in all the medical records, produced and got marked by the petitioner as Ex.P.7, 10 and 15, his age is mentioned as 20 years.

The age of the petitioner is not specifically denied by the respondent and even, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record, to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner is considered as 20 years, as on the date of accident.

a) Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of both bones of left leg.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries caused to the petitioner he found that, there is 34% permanent physical disability of the left lower limb and 17%
permanent physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.10 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 case-sheets (total 2), Ex.P.16 x-rays (total 4),

7
Ex.P.17 OPD record and Ex.P.18 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner had sustained the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability suffered by the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 20-06-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 15-08-2024,
which is after lapse of two years and one month from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that,
the fractures sustained by the petitioner are united and the condition of the petitioner was stable at the time of his clinical examination.

Therefore, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner,
injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 14% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 14% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
b) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was student and also working as electrician and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was student and also working as electrician and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
c)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 20 years is 18.

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 14/100 X 18 = Rs.4,68,720/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 11 medical bills, as per Ex.P.12.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.66,191/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.66,191/- under the head of medical expenses.

viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 20 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of both bones of left leg.
Further, he has suffered permanent physical disability to the extent of 14% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.3 has not issued estimation of cost for said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. While answering Issue No.1, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that,
there is contributory negligence to the extent of 30% on the part of the petitioner and 70% on the Maneesh K.S vs Umesha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135360493/
9 part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HN-1470.
Therefore, the respondent is liable to pay only 70% out of total compensation amount.

Accordingly, it is held that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 4,68,720-00 2.
Medical expenses 66,191-00 3. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 4.
Attendant charges 7,000-00
5. Food and nourishment 5,600-00 6. Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00 9.

Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 7,08,511-00 70% of Total Rs.
4,95,958-00

For the reasons stated supra, as the petitioner is held liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 30%, after deducting the said value from the total compensation amount, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,95,958/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04-HN- 1470 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the usage of said vehicle.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But, there is no cogent and corroborative evidence placed on record to show that, the accident has taken place due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, at the relevant point of time of accident, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-04- HN-1470 was riding his motorcycle with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and carrying three pillion riders on the said motorcycle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
But, the petitioner has unequivocally admitted in his cross-examination that, to attend the nature call he had parked his motorcycle on the national highway and in order to reach the service road he jumped the concrete barricade installed at both the ends of the said national highway and after attending the nature call he was returning towards his parked motorcycle by crossing the service road, from the place where there were no zebra cross marks to cross the road.
The above admissions given by the petitioner clearly establishes the negligence of the petitioner and it clearly goes to show that, the petitioner was not diligent and taken required care and caution while crossing the public road and thereby contributed in the cause of accident.
If the petitioner had taken required care and caution while using the public road, having proper lookout at the movement of vehicles on the said road, the accident could not have occurred.
On the other hand, if the rider of offending motorcycle had rode his motorcycle slowly or in moderate speed, with due care and caution, following the traffic rules and regulations, he could have avoided the said accident.
The rider of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and observe traffic rules and regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.
Further,
the oral and documentary evidence available on record by both the sides clearly goes to show that,
the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle is at higher side, than that of the petitioner.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent to show that,
the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN-1470 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
